name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to attempt access to accounts when passwords or PINs are unknown.
applicable_event_evidence: Multiple authentication failures in a single session, rapid authentication retry sequences, or credential dictionary attempts.

name: Password Guessing
description: Adversaries may attempt to guess passwords of accounts to gain access.
applicable_event_evidence: Repeated failed login attempts targeting the same username or service over a short duration.

name: System Owner/User Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to identify the primary user, currently logged-in user, prior logged-in users, or set of users that commonly use a system.
applicable_event_evidence: Execution of commands querying user identity or logged in sessions: whoami, id, w, who, users, last, logname, cat /etc/passwd.

name: System Information Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to get detailed information about the operating system and hardware, including version, patches, system architecture, etc.
applicable_event_evidence: Execution of commands enumerating OS version, architecture, or hardware: uname, /etc/os-release, lscpu, /proc/cpuinfo, systeminfo.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
description: Adversaries may abuse Unix shells to execute arbitrary commands and scripts.
applicable_event_evidence: Shell executions or interactive sessions invoking /bin/sh, /bin/bash, dash, or piped shell commands.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.
applicable_event_evidence: PowerShell executions, encoded command lines (-enc), or cmdlets such as Invoke-Expression and Invoke-WebRequest.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services and open ports that are available on hosts across a network.
applicable_event_evidence: Port scanning, SYN packet sweeps, or multi-port probes against network decoy ports.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment.
applicable_event_evidence: Payloads downloading external binaries or scripts via curl, wget, ftp, tftp, certutil, bitsadmin.

name: Scheduled Task/Job: Cron
description: Adversaries may abuse the cron utility to execute malicious code on a scheduled or recurring basis.
applicable_event_evidence: Writing or editing crontabs (/etc/crontab, /etc/cron.*, crontab -e, crontab -l) or systemd timers.

name: Indicator Removal: File Deletion
description: Adversaries may delete files left behind by the actions of their software or clear logs to obscure their presence.
applicable_event_evidence: Commands deleting artifacts or clearing traces: rm -rf, shred, history -c, unset HISTFILE, truncate.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.
applicable_event_evidence: Successful login events (login_success, auth_success) establishing authenticated honeynet sessions.

name: File and Directory Discovery
description: Adversaries may enumerate files and directories or search in specific locations of the host for certain information.
applicable_event_evidence: Commands traversing directories or locating files: ls -la, dir /s, find / -name.

name: Remote System Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of other systems on the network.
applicable_event_evidence: Commands enumerating neighbors: arp -a, ping -c, net view, ip neigh.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries may attempt to take advantage of a software vulnerability in an Internet-facing computer or system to gain access.
applicable_event_evidence: Inbound HTTP payloads exhibiting SQL injection syntax, directory traversal ('../'), Log4j expressions ('${jndi:'), or known CVE exploit signatures.
